key_highlights: RBA issues blunt warning ahead of next rate decision; IMF urges spending cuts as another hike looms, pressuring rate-sensitive sectors
ASX limped through a volatile week but closed on gains as oil prices and bond yields eased; big four banks advanced
Recession odds for 2027 rising, driven by sticky inflation, petrol price shock, and housing unaffordability
Iron ore prices under pressure ('iron ore roaches seethe'), weighing on BHP, RIO, FMG
Japan diverts Australian LNG to domestic use as East Coast starves, creating export revenue headwinds for energy majors
Anthropic secures $31bn datacentre deal in western Queensland, a structural positive for Australian tech/infrastructure
Coles maintains elevated milk prices despite axing farmer support, signalling consumer staples margin pressure
Qantas ground staff strike looms over Joyce-era bargaining agreements, adding operational risk to QAN.AX
Warren Buffett steps down as Berkshire chairman at 96, marking a generational shift in global value investing

sectors.trend: Iron ore prices under sustained pressure; gold explorers (Forrestania, Aurum) show prefeasibility progress but remain speculative. Commodity headwinds weigh on BHP, RIO, FMG.
sectors.implications: Near-term earnings risk for iron ore majors; gold juniors offer optionality but carry execution risk. Monitor iron ore contract pricing and China demand signals.

sectors.trend: Big four banks advanced on the week as bond yields eased, but RBA hawkishness and IMF spending-cut warnings threaten net interest margin expansion. Housing unaffordability constrains credit growth.
sectors.implications: CBA, NAB, ANZ, WBC benefit from yield easing short-term but face policy headwinds. Housing stress could elevate NPLs in 2027.

sectors.trend: Oil prices easing provides relief to input costs but Japan diverting Australian LNG domestically threatens export revenue. Victoria retreats from renewable transmission, adding policy uncertainty. Petrol price shock hits consumers.
sectors.implications: Woodside, Santos face LNG export headwinds. Coal policy ambiguity (Albo course) creates regulatory risk for energy transition plays. Petrol shock pressures transport and consumer discretionary.

sectors.trend: Coles maintains elevated milk prices post-farmer support removal, squeezing household budgets. EV adoption accelerating as consumers flee petrol prices. Housing unaffordability suppresses discretionary spend.
sectors.implications: WES, WOW face margin pressure from input costs. EV transition benefits battery/charging infrastructure names. Consumer staples defensive positioning warranted.

sectors.trend: Anthropic's $31bn Queensland datacentre deal signals structural AI infrastructure buildout in Australia. AI adoption concerns persist among workforce. Generac's Amazon datacentre deal globally reinforces AI capex cycle.
sectors.implications: Long-term positive for Australian datacentre REITs and infrastructure funds. Short-term AI disruption risk to services sector employment.

sectors.trend: Qantas ground staff strike threat over Joyce-era agreements adds operational risk. Petrol price shock impacts logistics costs across supply chains.
sectors.implications: QAN.AX faces near-term disruption risk. Freight and logistics margins under pressure from fuel costs.

key_themes: RBA hawkish pivot and IMF fiscal warnings create a tightening monetary/fiscal backdrop
2027 recession probability rising, driven by inflation stickiness and housing stress
Commodity complex under pressure: iron ore weak, LNG export diversion, oil easing
Housing unaffordability at extreme levels, constraining credit and consumer confidence
AI infrastructure buildout (Anthropic $31bn) as a structural growth theme
Consumer squeeze: petrol shock, milk price hikes, unaffordable housing
Global risk-off: Buffett succession, Middle East oil shock risk, US Fed hike

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA rate hike / IMF fiscal tightening
risk_assessment.mitigation: Overweight short-duration bonds; reduce leverage; favour rate-insensitive sectors (healthcare, staples)
Maintain cash buffer; diversify into defensive equities (CSL, WES); avoid cyclical overexposure
Reduce BHP/RIO/FMG weight; rotate into gold (defensive commodity) and energy
Avoid QAN.AX ahead of strike; monitor alternative transport plays

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Middle East oil shock / geopolitical escalation
risk_assessment.mitigation: Hedge with energy equities and gold; monitor Brent crude and AUD/USD
Underweight REITs and construction; favour banks with strong NPL provisioning

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold equities as inflation hedge and safe haven amid recession fears
opportunities.rationale: RBA hawkishness, IMF warnings, and geopolitical risk support gold; Forrestania and Aurum prefeasibility progress adds catalyst

opportunities.recommendation: Position in Australian datacentre / AI infrastructure beneficiaries
opportunities.rationale: Anthropic $31bn Queensland deal signals multi-year capex cycle; structural demand for power and infrastructure

opportunities.recommendation: Tactical overweight big four banks on yield easing
opportunities.rationale: Banks advanced as bond yields fell; NIM expansion potential if RBA pauses after next hike

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce exposure to iron ore majors; trim BHP/RIO/FMG
defensive_moves.rationale: Iron ore prices under sustained pressure; China demand concerns; commodity headwinds

defensive_moves.recommendation: Increase cash and short-duration bond allocation
defensive_moves.rationale: RBA hike risk and IMF fiscal tightening create near-term volatility; preserve capital ahead of potential recession

defensive_moves.recommendation: Avoid QAN.AX ahead of potential strike; underweight transport
defensive_moves.rationale: Ground staff strike threat over Joyce-era agreements creates binary operational risk

defensive_moves.recommendation: Underweight REITs and construction; favour healthcare defensives
defensive_moves.rationale: Housing unaffordability at extreme levels; credit stress risk; CSL offers defensive earnings visibility

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain volatile and range-bound. RBA rate decision and IMF fiscal warnings dominate. Oil/bond yield easing provides temporary support but iron ore weakness and recession fears cap upside. Expect 2-4% index volatility. Banks and defensives outperform; materials and cyclicals lag.
market_outlook.long_term: 2027 recession risk is the dominant macro narrative. Housing unaffordability and sticky inflation constrain RBA easing. Structural positives in AI infrastructure (Anthropic deal) and energy transition offer selective opportunities. A gradual ASX grind lower to 8,000-8,500 range is plausible if recession materialises; 9,500+ requires a commodity upcycle or policy pivot.

Iron ore contract pricing and China stimulus signals
US Fed rate decision and global bond yield trajectory
Australian CPI and employment data releases
Middle East geopolitical developments / oil supply
watch_list: RBA cash rate and statement (next meeting)
Brent crude and Australian LNG spot prices
